To determine how many peaks are part of the molecular ion cluster for the molecule CBr4 in its mass spectrum, we need to consider the isotopic composition of bromine.

Bromine has two stable isotopes: Br-79 and Br-81, with natural abundances of approximately 50.7% and 49.3%, respectively. In the mass spectrum of a compound like CBr4, each bromine atom can be either Br-79 or Br-81, leading to a variety of isotopic combinations.

For CBr4, which contains four bromine atoms, the possible combinations and corresponding peaks in the mass spectrum are as follows:

1. All Br-79 (79-79-79-79)
2. Three Br-79 and one Br-81 (79-79-79-81)
3. Two Br-79 and two Br-81 (79-79-81-81)
4. One Br-79 and three Br-81 (79-81-81-81)
5. All Br-81 (81-81-81-81)

Therefore, the molecular ion cluster for CBr4 will have 5 peaks corresponding to these combinations.
